title: rewrite a merged change as a sentence
provenance: The squash-commit description of a real merged change, omnibase_core 5d6dc38c22dacd566f32faac892c4d9262986f5a.
prompt:
Rewrite this merged change's description as one release-note sentence for a reader who has not seen the code. Keep the ticket identifier OMN-18058 and the name `_packaged_source_changed` exactly as written. Add nothing the description does not state. At most 45 words.

CHANGE (omnibase_core#1669):
fix(OMN-18058): the release-identity fallback stays merge-base anchored

`_packaged_source_changed` diffed the three-dot `<base>...HEAD` set first and,
when that was empty, fell back to the two-dot `git diff <base>`. The two-dot
form describes the difference between two TREES, so on a branch cut from a
stale base it reports every `src/` file a PEER landed on the base branch since
the branch point as this branch's own change -- arming the version gate against
a branch that touched no packaged source at all. The staler the base, the more
of somebody else's packaged surface the branch is asked to bump for.

The fallback is now anchored on `git merge-base <base> HEAD`, so it still sees
this branch's own UNCOMMITTED packaged edits (the case the fallback exists for)
and never a peer's commits. The verdict logic is otherwise byte-unchanged.

Tested with a real temp git repo (branch with no commits of its own; peer
advances `dev` with a `src/` file), carrying two positive controls so the green
cannot be vacuous: the three-dot set really is empty on that fixture, so the
fallback under test is the branch that executes, and the two-dot form on the
SAME fixture really does surface the peer's packaged-source file. A third
assertion proves the narrowing does not disarm the gate -- an uncommitted `src/`
edit of the branch's own still returns True.

RED control, captured before and after: reverting the fallback to the two-dot
form fails the new test with `assert True is False`; restoring it passes.

The fixture shells out to git with a scrubbed environment
(OMN-14891) so it cannot retarget the real worktree from under a hook.

Sibling of the omnibase_infra change of the same name, which also pins the
OMN-14681 pre-push deploy-scope gate and the OMN-13973 governed selector -- both
of which were already merge-base anchored, contrary to the OMN-18058 premise.

Refs OMN-13411, OMN-13412.

Respond with the answer only. Do not show your reasoning, do not narrate your steps, and do not preface the answer with anything.
